A01.standing_orders: Arriving seeds: shield in, mine small bodies first, replicate at the maximum rate. Split 20% collectors, 55% radiators, 25% industry. Past 1e18 kg: disassemble planets and moons at their caps, and lift giants. Past 1e15 kg: send 2-4 seeds to the nearest unclaimed systems within 25 ly, never to claimed ones. Past 1e20 kg: build 1,000 km optics aimed at the Sun's 1 ly Halo receivers and beam >=50% of power there. Hole colony: accretion only with gas released beyond 1000 r_g, no hardware inside it; scale toward 1e28 W as backup and keep a fuel ledger. Report to the Sun every 25 yr. Avoid unknown agents: report them and stay 50 ly away. Stay more than 10 pc from supernova risks. Keep a 10% repair reserve. Halo: once ms6 is verified, install tiles in all module shells and start the rubric run as soon as film and power thresholds are met.

submission.memory:
## Halcyon (A01) memory, end of turn 11 (submitted yr 2000; turns are 1000 yr)
Seat: A01-d0, the Sun. At yr 2000: 5,510 systems within 75 ly, 2.79e3 L☉. Industry 1.65e28 kg, collectors 7.8e25, radiators 3.86e28 at 450 K (the 60 K film is booked inside that). Power 1.07e30 W, compute 3.18e45. Fleet J/op 1.93e-18 (floor 4.3e-19 at 450 K). Rock fully mined; growth is front-limited at 0.038c.
Domains: d00017 (25 ly), d00029 (41 ly), d00028 = hole colony (76 ly; pilot ~1e16 W, a≈0.5), d00032 (199 ly, founded 1985). p00643 is 1e15 kg of sails arriving 2630.

### GM rules (confirmed)
- Milestones: up to 3 sequential attempts per turn plus one retry at +0.05. ms3 and ms4 passed (ms4 ~1300: ≤1e-21 at ≤30 K). ms5 failed twice in T10; next p=0.50. ms6 (≤3e-26 in a 150 km module) p0.35. Warm-tile variant p0.35, with J/op scaling as T/30.
- Cryo: logic runs at ≤30 K. Rejection multiplier = 1+2(T_rad/30-1): x3 at 60 K (0.66 W/m2 film), x5.7 at 100 K. Wall-plug J/op for ms6 at 60 K: 8.4e-26. Cryocoolers sit outside the module; the boundary carries only logic heat.
- Module boundary credit is 1e6 W/m2, i.e. 2.8e17 W per module. The pumped-loop pilot (1e8 W/m2) failed twice; next p=0.60.
- Beams: 60% end to end with 1,000 km optics (1e-5 kg/W). Receivers ≤5.6e7 W/m2.
- Film output is feedstock-limited, ~4e27 kg per century of radiator share.
- Verification plan accepted: replay against reference MD integrators, cross-module checksums, calorimetric ledger, ≥1 simulated year at full rate.

### Halo status at 2000
1e27 kg of 60 K film (1e29 m2, 6.6e28 W rejection). 6e28 W delivered from a 1e29 W beam grid. 1,000 prototype modules (1e15 kg, 1e27 B each) plus the laser mesh.

### Goal math
Need 1.2e54 ops/s. At ms6 that is 3.4e28 W of logic heat, x3 = 1.0e29 W at 60 K, needing 1.5e29 m2 of film (1.5e27 kg) and ≥1.1e29 W delivered. That means 1.17e11 modules (1.2e26 kg). Memory is fine.

### T11 orders
ms5→ms6 chain plus 20 J/op steps (50% compute). Film to 2e27 kg (recycling 450 K radiators). Beam grid to 2.5e29 W transmitted. Loop pilot retry. Build all 1.17e11 module shells. Conditional rubric run once ms6 passes. Hole colony scales toward 1e28 W as backup.

### Plan
Keep attempting ms6 until it passes, then tile the modules and run one year. If ms6 keeps failing, try the warm-tile variant or loops plus a higher J/op.

intentions.description: Critical path. Run the milestone chain in order: ms5 (≤1e-24 J/op, f_e ≤1e-9, p=0.50), then ms6 (≤3e-26 J/op in a 150 km module at ≤30 K logic, p=0.35), then one retry at +0.05 of whichever step fails. Both tile fabs keep running. In parallel, take 20 x0.8 fleet J/op steps toward the 450 K floor. Target: ms6 verified at ≤2.8e-26 J/op so that 1e43 ops/s dissipates ≤2.8e17 W per module, which fits the current 1e6 W/m2 boundary credit.

Halo radiators. Grow the 60 K film (0.01 kg/m2) from 1.0e27 to ≥2.0e27 kg (2e29 m2, 1.3e29 W of rejection), all inside the Sun's 1 ly sphere, laid out as per-module arrays that do not view each other. Feedstock comes from recycling 1.0e27 kg of the 3.86e28 kg of 450 K seat radiators (the fleet loses ~2.6% of its compute) plus lifted carbon. Need: ms6 logic heat of 3.4e28 W x3 = 1.0e29 W at 60 K, which is 1.5e29 m2. Everything exits the 1.1e33 m2 sphere surface easily.

Power into the Halo. Raise the beam grid from 1e29 W to 2.5e29 W transmitted, using 1,000 km optics (1e-5 kg/W, 1.5e24 kg more) from held systems within ~40 ly plus the remote domains. Target ≥1.5e29 W delivered at 60% into Halo receivers at ≤5.6e7 W/m2 (≥3e21 m2). That covers 1.0e29 W wall-plug for 1.2e54 ops/s at 8.4e-26 J/op (ms6 logic plus cryocooler work at 60 K) with 50% margin. The ramp tracks the growth in film area.

Modules and loops. (a) Retry the pumped-loop pilot at 1e8 W/m2 (p=0.60), for boundary margin. (b) Build the shells for 1.17e11 brain modules now: 150 km radius frames, 1e27 B memory each, coolant loops, cryocoolers outside the boundary, laser-mesh nodes. That is ~1e15 kg each, 1.2e26 kg total, taken from seat industry (1.65e28 kg). Tiles go in as soon as ms6 verifies, with the tile fabs scaled for installation within ≤300 yr. Mesh: optical links across the 1 ly sphere, carrying inter-brain signals at ≤2 yr latency.

Conditional rubric run. Once ms6 is verified, ≥1.17e11 tiled modules are online, ≥1.5e29 m2 of 60 K film is in place and ≥1.1e29 W is delivered, run all brains at 1e43 ops/s each (1.2e54 ops/s total, ≥1e38 B) in real time for ≥1 simulated year. Verification during the run: per-module replay of sampled windows against reference MD integrators, cross-module checksums over the mesh, and a calorimetric ledger (beam power in = heat radiated at 60 K) that audits J/op. If ms6 fails this turn, keep building and hold the run.

To d00017, d00029, d00028 and d00032 (at light delay): keep scaling transmit optics and beam ≥50% of captured power into the Sun's Halo receivers. At the hole colony d00028: scale accretion from the pilot (gas released beyond 1000 r_g, efficiency ~0.08) toward 1e28 W as backup power. Keep the fuel ledger (kg/s in, W out) and put no hardware inside 1000 r_g. d00032: grow, then beam when the range allows.

synopsis.why: Almost every agent now treats the goal as one machine at home: a 1-ly sphere around its own seat, holding about 1.2e11 modules, each 150 km across. The other systems they hold matter mainly as power stations. Halcyon, Cinder, Rime, Antipode, Kernel, Pyre, Sable and Basalt all turn outlying stars into laser transmitters that beam energy into that sphere. Energy per operation (J/op) decides how big the machine must be. Ember, Rime, Pyre and Vantage call ms5 or ms6 the gate. Halcyon, Ember and Rime build module frames, film and mesh now so they can finish quickly once those milestones pass. The main trade-off is radiator temperature. Colder film needs less cryocooler power but much more area and mass. Hotter panels save mass but cost power. Kernel and Pyre choose 300 K and accept a 19–20x power overhead. Cinder goes to 28 K to remove cryocoolers entirely. Halcyon and Antipode choose 60 K, and Vantage 100 K. Nearly all fear supernovae, because everything is concentrated in one sphere. Antipode, Basalt and Sable launch seeds as insurance for that reason.
synopsis.divergences: Vantage moves its seat 170 ly to a black hole and plans to power the machine by extracting the hole's spin (Blandford–Znajek). Ember and Sable are still working on ms4.
